content_blocks.label: lead_paragraph
content_blocks.text: A new immigration reform proposal introduced by the federal government has been met with strong opposition from border states, which argue that it does not adequately address security concerns.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_1
content_blocks.text: The bill includes provisions for increased funding for border security and expedited deportation processes. However, state officials from Texas and Arizona are pushing back against the plan.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_2
content_blocks.text: Governor Mark Davis of Texas said, 'We need more robust measures to secure our borders before we can consider any reforms.'

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_3
content_blocks.text: Rep. Luis Rodriguez added, 'This proposal is a step in the right direction, but we need to see concrete actions to prevent illegal crossings.'

content_blocks.label: pull_quote
content_blocks.text: We need more robust measures to secure our borders before we can consider any reforms.
